checks.note: There are exactly three days (Day 1, Day 2 and Day 3), each with a morning-to-evening schedule.
Every day has a named breakfast, lunch, afternoon snack or drink stop, and dinner. Day 3 is built around Jean-Talon Market. Sightseeing fills the gaps between food stops.

There's one splurge (Au Pied de Cochon, ~$90-120). The rest are mid-priced spots like Schwartz's, La Banquise, L'Express and Brasserie T!. The food total of ~$350-440 per person for 3 days fits a mid-range budget.

It covers fall foliage spots (Mont-Royal, McGill, Parc La Fontaine), gives rain plans for each day, and notes harvest season at Jean-Talon (apples, cider). It also flags Canadian Thanksgiving closures on Oct 12, 2026, and that date is correct.

It names real places with addresses, such as St-Viateur Bagel, Olimpico, Schwartz's, Dieu du Ciel!, Au Pied de Cochon, Olive + Gourmando, Time Out Market, Myriade, Hof Kelsten, Fromagerie Hamel, La Banquise and L'Express. It also says to confirm that Brasserie T! is still open.
